articles.title: A Master's Degree in Astronomy
articles.summary: Paul Kohlmiller recounts his 4.5-year journey to earning an online Master's Degree in Astronomy from Swinburne University, inspired by Marni Berendsen. He details the program's rigorous structure, which included 12 classes with extensive readings, online discussions, two research papers, and open-book tests, contrasting it with 'paper mill' degrees. Kohlmiller reflects on the time, financial investment, and academic challenges, ultimately noting the difficulty in quantifying its worth but emphasizing the personal achievement.

articles.title: The Shallow Sky
articles.summary: This article details celestial observing opportunities for December, highlighting Jupiter's close passes with Neptune, a double shadow transit, and its daytime visibility, alongside updates on Mercury, Mars, and Saturn. It also explores the utility of Twitter for tracking real-time space news, like the Mars rovers' status and the LCROSS water discovery. The author briefly reflects on the value of an Astronomy Master's degree for amateur astronomers.

articles.title: Staring at Lightning
articles.summary: This article emphasizes the scientific value of monitoring lightning, not just for its visual spectacle but as a key indicator of storm dynamics and potential climate change. NASA and NOAA are developing the Geostationary Lightning Mapper (GLM) for the GOES-R geostationary satellite, set to launch around 2015. GLM will provide continuous, wide-area lightning data, offering unprecedented insights for climate research, severe weather forecasting, and aviation safety, overcoming limitations of previous observational methods.

articles.title: The Last Month In Astronomy
articles.summary: This past month in astronomy brought updates on the Hayabusa mission's challenging return with asteroid samples, alongside groundbreaking discoveries. Researchers identified a new class of rapid supernova, found a dense carbon atmosphere on a neutron star, and observed the most distant galaxy cluster yet. Furthermore, 32 new exoplanets were discovered, including potential super-Earths in habitable zones, and new images of galaxies and stellar nurseries were captured.

articles.title: It Must Be Astronomical...
articles.summary: The December 2009 SJAA Ephemeris newsletter details a telescope loaner program and two astronomy job openings at the Astronomical Society of the Pacific and Lick Observatory. It also announces upcoming events like the Geminid meteor shower and the SJAA Holiday Party, provides an astronomical fact about the Andromeda Galaxy, and lists club officers and contact information.
